big-news.text: Høyre's alternative 2027 budget cuts about 25 billion kr in taxes and fees. That includes a work deduction worth about 7,700 kr less tax for everyone with a job, plus a lower wealth tax. It's an opposition proposal, not law.
PST, the security police, expects Russian intelligence to try sabotage in Norway in the coming year, possibly including attacks that could cost lives.
The Amadeus leak exposed data on 144,249 Norwegian and Widerøe passengers. If you've flown with either, watch for phishing.

whats-changing.text: Flu and COVID cases are rising, and FHI (the public health institute) says it's getting urgent to get vaccinated if you're eligible.

oslo.text: Oslo S is a mess this morning. A goods train derailed last night and blocked tracks 1–5, and then an electrical fault shut the station completely just after 06:00. Some trains were running again around 07:00 and some routes have replacement buses, so check the Vy or Flytoget app.
Yesterday's snow stopped every inner-city bus in the morning. Ruter says the T-bane is the safest bet while the roads are bad.
A heated year-round sea pool for about 35–40 people is coming to Sukkerbiten on a 36 m barge. If all goes to plan, it opens in about a year.
The city has finally funded the Maridalen bike path after a 45-year wait.

be-aware.text: The snow warning is over and today looks mostly sunny, but roads can still be icy, so allow extra time on the road.
Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft services had problems overnight, and Microsoft is working on a fix. That's worth knowing if Teams acts up today.

fun-and-free.text: Top pick: The Kunstbok Oslo art book fair is at the National Library (Solli plass) on Saturday and Sunday from 11:00 to 18:00. It has 100 exhibitors and talks, Iceland is the guest country, and entry is free.
Ekebergsletta parkrun is a free 5 km on Saturday at 09:30.
Sentralen has a free Roller Disco on Saturday at 15:00.
*Support Structures* opens at Kunstnernes Hus tonight at 19:00, with free entry.
Navaranaaq is music and literature on Sunday at 15:00, with free tickets.
